title: Automated Pre-install Gate: Quota, IAM, DNS, GPU & Upgrade-readiness Validator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Build an automated, idempotent pre-install validator for Redwood Private installs (VPC/offline) that runs as part of the installer CI and as a preflight step for customers. The validator will query cloud provider APIs and local node info to ensure: account quotas are sufficient (GPUs, vCPUs, ENIs), required IAM roles/policies exist and have necessary permissions, DNS zones and delegation are resolvable, and the target cluster has the expected GPU types, drivers, and node-level prerequisites for upgrades and runtime.

Goal: fail fast with clear remediation guidance and machine-readable output (JSON) so both install automation and our support tooling (Console onboarding, Solutions) can act on results. This reduces failed installs and support cycles for private deployments and enforces upgrade-readiness checks before we schedule rolling upgrades or image changes.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight binary (or Terraform-integrated check) can be invoked with a single command and returns structured JSON exit status and human-readable summary.
Validator checks quotas for common cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP) for configured regions and reports exact missing resources and recommended instance types/quotas to request.
IAM checks identify missing permissions and provide example least-privilege policy snippets linking to our Confluence policy templates.
DNS checks detect delegation issues, missing records for load balancers, and common misconfigurations (private zone vs public zone) with remediation steps.
GPU capacity checks verify presence of expected GPU SKUs, minimum driver/kernel versions, NVIDIA/CUDA compatibility, and warn on fractional packing issues that can cause OOMs.
Upgrade-readiness checks validate node OS/kernel versions, docker/containerd versions, kubelet compatibility matrix for target runtime version, and report blocking items.
Implemented as an installer-stage hook and as a reusable Terraform external data source so customers can run preflight via CI/CD or interactively.
Integration tests added to installer CI showing the validator catching at least 3 real misconfigurations (quota shortfall, missing IAM scope, DNS delegation error).
Documentation and runbook (Confluence) published and linked; support playbook created for interpreting validator output.
implementation_steps: Spike: prototype provider-agnostic quota & IAM checks (Go) that call AWS/Azure/GCP APIs and output JSON (ETA 2d).
Design: define canonical JSON schema for preflight results and mapping to Console onboarding UI (schema doc + examples).
Engineer: implement DNS resolver checks and LB record expectations (ingress/egress) and unit tests (3d).
Engineer: implement GPU SKU & driver scanning via SSH/agent and cloud capacity queries; include fallback heuristics for spot/heterogeneous pools (4d).
Integrate: add Terraform external data source wrapper and an installer hook so 'terraform apply' can call and fail-fast on preflight failures.
CI: add negative test cases to installer CI pipeline using a mocked cloud account (or vendor-supplied test accounts) to ensure checks detect problems.
Docs: publish Confluence runbook, sample least-priv policy, and support triage steps; add examples to docs.redwood.ai/private/preflight.
Rollout: enable validator in canary installs with opt-out flag for 2 weeks, gather metrics on false positives/negatives, then flip required bit.
